record.paper_title: Open problems in graph theory. II: On the achromatic number of a graph
record.context_brief: Achromatic number decision problem for trees
record.original_question: Given a finite tree T = (V,E) and a positive integer K, does T admit a complete K-coloring, meaning a coloring of the vertices of T with colors {1,2,...,K} such that adjacent vertices receive different colors and, for every pair i,j of distinct colors, some edge of T has one endpoint colored i and the other endpoint colored j?

evidence.quote: INSTANCE: A tree T = (V,E), a positive integer K. QUESTION: Does T have a complete K-coloring? A coloring of the vertices of a tree T with K colors {1,2,...,K} is called complete if (i) adjacent vertices are assigned different colors, and (ii) for every pair i,j of distinct colors there exists a pair of adjacent vertices colored i and j.

UPDATE: this problem has been shown to be NP-complete for trees; I will provide the reference shortly. It now remains to determine for what classes of trees can the achromatic number be determined in polynomial time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T=(V,E)$ be a finite tree and let $K$ be a positive integer. A complete $K$-coloring of $T$ is a map $c:V\to\{1,2,\dots,K\}$ satisfying:
(i) for every edge $\{u,v\}\in E$, $c(u)\neq c(v)$ (properness); and
(ii) for every pair $i\neq j$ in $\{1,2,\dots,K\}$, there exists an edge $\{u,v\}\in E$ with $\{c(u),c(v)\}=\{i,j\}$.

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given $(T,K)$ as input, decide whether $T$ admits a complete $K$-coloring.
artifact.status_search_result: The decision problem of whether a tree admits a complete K-coloring (i.e., whether the achromatic number of a tree is at least K) was shown to be NP-complete by Cairnie and Edwards (and independently by Manlove and McDiarmid). Polynomial-time algorithms are known for restricted subclasses, e.g., trees of bounded maximum degree.

status_evidence.title: Complete coloring - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Determining the achromatic number is NP-hard; testing whether it is greater than a given number is NP-complete, even for trees.
status_evidence.claim: The achromatic-number decision problem is NP-complete for trees.

status_evidence.title: The achromatic number of bounded degree trees
status_evidence.snippet: A polynomial-time algorithm exists for determining the achromatic number of a tree with bounded maximum degree.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time algorithms exist for trees of bounded degree, complementing the general NP-completeness result.
